page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7t.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 6 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration delivers 96.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core memory-to-vCPU ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the instance in the average tier across most metrics. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU performance scores are 1893.38 and 11663.11, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show 642.92 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 78.47 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In database operations, the instance achieves a PassMark database score of 5826.28 and handles 11.97 million Redis SET operations per second.

The dedicated CPU allocation and high memory density offer resource efficiency for RAM-bound workloads, though the lack of bundled local storage requires external block storage integration. While the instance handles smaller workloads efficiently, it exhibits performance limitations on larger computational tasks. For example, LLM inference prompt processing with a medium 7B model drops to a weak tier at 24.29 tokens/second, though text generation remains average at 9.4 tokens/second. This instance is appropriate for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications requiring substantial RAM without local disk dependencies.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7t.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 12 dedicated vCPUs and 96.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor, this instance provides an 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks generally fall within the average range, with a single-core Geekbench score of 1599.0 and a multi-core score of 7867.0. It processes 11.97 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves a static web serving throughput of 16.92 GB/sec. However, a key tradeoff is its weak performance in medium 7B LLM prompt processing, which registers at 24.29 tokens/second. This instance is appropriate for memory-intensive applications, caching layers, and database operations that do not require local NVMe storage.
